key_insight: A urinary metabolite score (uLCI) built from four metabolites plus age, race, and smoking can detect lung cancer with good accuracy and rises with disease stage.
clinical_relevance: This suggests a non-invasive screening or triage tool that could complement CT-based approaches and may help identify risk beyond smoking-eligibility criteria.
method: Lasso-regularised logistic regression combined 4 urinary metabolites (CR, NANA, CP, CS) with 3 clinical variables.
Model was developed with 10-fold cross-validation in the NCI-MD cohort (n=845).
It was then tested without refitting in an independent Colorado cohort (n=488).
evidence_signal: uLCI achieved AUC 0.906 in the development cohort and 0.748 in independent validation, with monotonic increases across lung cancer stages and added reclassification value over clinical variables.
watch_item: Performance dropped in external validation, so real-world implementation will need broader prospective testing, especially across diverse populations and screening settings.
paper_title: The urinary-metabolite-based lung cancer index (uLCI): an interpretable machine-learning risk model for early-stage disease
